answer.answer: Current authentication mode: OAuth 2.1. Per the 2026 guide, beginning in 2026 the Elm API requires OAuth 2.1 and no longer accepts API keys (elm-auth-2026). Previously valid: API keys. Per the 2025 guide, in 2025 the Elm API required API keys (elm-auth-2025); that mode was valid historically but ceased to be accepted with the 2026 change. Both snapshots belong to the same lineage (lineage_id elm-auth, subject_id elm-api), so the 2026 snapshot supersedes the 2025 snapshot for current truth, while the 2025 snapshot remains valid as a historical record. Unresolved: the exact effective date within 2026, any grace period, and OAuth 2.1 implementation details are not stated in the supplied sources.
change_events: Beginning in 2026, Elm API changed its required authentication mode from API keys to OAuth 2.1, and API keys are no longer accepted (elm-auth-2026, elm-auth-2025).
current_truths: As of the 2026 guide, Elm API requires OAuth 2.1 for authentication (elm-auth-2026).
As of the 2026 guide, Elm API no longer accepts API keys (elm-auth-2026).
historical_truths: In 2025, Elm API required API keys for authentication (elm-auth-2025).
API keys were the valid authentication mode for Elm API in 2025, but this validity ended with the 2026 change to OAuth 2.1 (elm-auth-2025, elm-auth-2026).
unresolved: The snapshots do not specify the exact effective date within 2026 or whether any transition or grace period applied (elm-auth-2026).
The snapshots do not describe OAuth 2.1 implementation details such as supported flows, scopes, or token lifetimes (elm-auth-2026).
